arrive.text: A room, two boxes, and something that has never once been wrong.

predictor.text: It predicted what you would choose, before you came in. Yesterday.

box_a.text: The glass box holds a thousand. You can see it.

box_b.text: The closed box holds a million, but only if it predicted you'd take the closed box alone. If it predicted you'd take both, it's empty.

filled.text: The boxes were filled yesterday. The money is already in the room, or it isn't.

causal.text: Nothing you do now can put the million in, or take it out.

ledger.text: Every visitor who took both boxes found the closed box empty. Every visitor who took only the closed box got the million.

ledger_look.text: Name after name. Both boxes, a thousand. One box, a million. Not a single exception.

one_2.text: It saw you coming. But the thousand was right there, and taking it couldn't have changed what was in the box. Could it?

both_1.text: The closed box is empty. A thousand.

both_2.text: Whatever it predicted was done yesterday. Taking both was bound to get you more than taking one. So why are you poorer?

again.text: The next day. The same room. But this time, both boxes are glass.

glass.text: You can see the million. It predicted you would still take only that box.

ask2.text: The money is right in front of you. One box, or both?

one2_1.text: You leave the thousand where it is, in plain sight, and take the million.

one2_2.text: Nothing was hidden this time, and nothing stopped you. You stayed the person it said you were.

both2_2.text: It has never been wrong before. Was it wrong about you? Or did seeing the money make you someone else?

end.text: About half of everyone takes one box, and half take both. Each half thinks the answer is obvious.
